scope_and_limits.scope: First-level battle + the existing linked shop only. Read-only inventory; no production art or code changed. Other levels are not changed or inventoried as accepted content.
scope_and_limits.status: Candidate/source audit, not user acceptance. No claim of pixel-identical reference reproduction or GPU/GL visual verification.
scope_and_limits.coordinate_conventions: All paths repository-relative. Crops are [x,y,width,height]; alpha bounding boxes are [left,top,right,bottom] with exclusive right/bottom. Unless stated otherwise anchors are crop-local source pixels; logical units refer to the 940x1672 canvas.
scope_and_limits.texture_sampling: No explicit CanvasItem.texture_filter override was found in scripts, scenes or project.godot. Sampling inherits Godot CanvasItem/viewport defaults. Project sets textures/default_filters/use_nearest_mipmap_filter=false but does not explicitly pin the default CanvasItem filter. AtlasTexture.filter_clip=true is set by the consumers; this is region edge clipping, not a nearest/linear choice. PNG import params below show compress/mode=0, mipmaps/generate=false, fix_alpha_border=true and premult_alpha=false. No import file is claimed to prove runtime GL behavior.
scope_and_limits.parent_transform: main.gd/startup.gd apply the uniform root canvas scale and letterbox below. Shop is a 940x1672 child of startup and does not apply a second root scale. Battle groups are neutral unless a role lists additional transforms. Animation, hit/recoil and UI transitions may temporarily alter transforms; base sizes are not final per-frame alpha silhouettes.
scope_and_limits.loading_contract: startup.gd HOME_RESOURCES preloads existing shared art. prepare_game_resources requests play.tscn, current layout background and target texture; new first-level cannon/card/deck/ball/ant assets are loaded by their actual runtime consumers. Listing a dependency does not imply it is in the startup preloading batch.
scope_and_limits.loading_chain_caveat: Shared33.5x33.5 board/cargo/stock/hopper/projectile draw rectangles are a scoped size contract, not proof of a complete visible unloading/loading chain. Existing bead_delivered feedback is a procedural transfer star and ring. Hopper visibility depends on live ammunition/projectile state.

frame_contract.interpretation: 1.531914894 is width ratio only. Runtime min() chooses1.531100478, yielding1439.234449761x2560 and0.38277512 horizontal pixels of margin on each side. Reference864x1536 is exactly9:16, logical940x1672 is slightly narrower. Do not stretch reference to force apparent alignment. Project viewport stretch keep may add further physical-window letterboxing on other window aspect ratios.

reference_evidence.role: Full approved references are comparison evidence only, never runtime backgrounds or assembled sprites. Presence does not imply current build acceptance.
reference_evidence.comparison_method: Read actual source, JSON/atlas crops, local import metadata and image alpha; visually inspect full references and clean background. Layout transforms are computed. Existing node export is optional structural evidence, explicitly offline composition. No new GPU render was executed by this inventory task.
reference_evidence.difference_policy: List semantic correspondence separately from observed differences and pending acceptance; do not infer exact reference dimensions for individual subjects without measured target crops.
reference_evidence.manual_difference_review: Battle composition review identifies rounder/gapped/larger-highlight candidate balls and side-facing full-body card ants instead of large front-facing portraits. Separate side stock differs from the reference filled-cannon composition. Empty hopper in the reviewed8-second offline state is state-dependent and is not a permanent-empty claim. Delivery has a symbolic5.5-radius transfer star, not a same-size ball handoff; offline shader approximation does not explain away these design differences.
reference_evidence.next_batch_boundary: Card portrait framing plus ball material and spacing are planned for the next batch. This inventory explicitly leaves them open and does not claim fixes.
